demo.banner: Demo — your edits reset on reload, and the AI assistant is scripted (no live model). In a real install you bring your own API key and pay your LLM provider for tokens.

templates.title: Entity templates
templates.hint: Named sheets: a field set plus a layout for display and print. Built-ins can be duplicated and edited for your own system.
templates.deleteConfirmBody: Template "{{name}}" will be deleted. Entities already created from it are unaffected.
templates.keyLocked: Field key is locked — already used in the layout
templates.removeFieldBody: Field "{{key}}" is used in {{count}} layout block(s) — they will be removed.
templates.inspectorEmpty: Select a block, region or field — its properties appear here.
templates.presetsNeedContainer: Add a columns or tabs region to insert presets into.
templates.problemNoType: Give the template an entity type
templates.problemBlankKey: One of the fields has a blank key — fill it in under Properties
templates.problemDuplicateKey: Two fields share a key — their values would overwrite each other
templates.modFormulaHint: value is the field's own score; other template fields can be referenced too

network.hairpinHint: Test this address from outside — a phone with Wi-Fi turned off, for instance. From inside your own network it often won't open, and that isn't a fault: most routers behave that way.
network.localHint: To let players connect from their own devices, close the app and start it again with start.bat --lan (players on your Wi-Fi) or start.bat --internet (players anywhere).
network.cgnat: Internet access isn't possible: your provider gave this connection the shared address {{ip}}, not one of your own (CGNAT). Ask them for a dedicated ("white") IP, or use Tailscale. Your local network still works.
network.noRouter: The router didn't answer the automatic port request — UPnP is most likely turned off in its settings. Turn it on, or forward the port by hand. Your local network still works.
network.refused: The router declined to forward the port. Forward it by hand in the router's settings. Your local network still works.
network.failed: Couldn't set up internet access. Your local network still works.
network.noTls: Traffic isn't encrypted — anyone between you and your players could read it. See docs/players.md to add a certificate.

play.linkInvalidBody: Ask your game master for a new invite link.
play.noCards: Nothing has been shared with you yet.

players.intro: Invite players to see the cards and board you reveal, and to keep their own notes.
players.linkOnce: This link is shown once. If it's lost, create a new one.
players.deleteBody: This player and all of their notes are removed for good. To keep the notes, revoke instead. Type the name to confirm.

updates.title: Updates
updates.restartHint: Close the app and run start.bat (or start.sh) again to update.
updates.dirty: There are local changes in the project folder, so it can't update automatically. Deal with them (git status), then relaunch.
updates.unavailable: Update checks aren't available for this install (downloaded as an archive, not a git clone).
updates.neverChecked: Not checked yet — it runs when the app starts.

projectSettings.heading: Project settings
projectSettings.instructionsPlaceholder: E.g. "Write NPC descriptions in the second person", "Always add a 'plot hook' field", "Keep a dark, gothic tone".
projectSettings.instructionsHint: Free-form notes on style, tone and format — blended into the assistant's and lore-generation system prompts for this project.
projectSettings.reindexHint: The search index is rebuilt from your entities automatically, but if the assistant can't find something that clearly exists, rebuilding it here fixes that.
projectSettings.deleteProjectHint: Permanently deletes all entities, relationships, knowledge base documents and attachments in this project.

usage.heading: Token usage
usage.hint: Cumulative token spend for this project across all AI assistant turns, lore generation and verification runs.

knowledge.heading: Project knowledge base
knowledge.hint: Upload reference documents (rulebooks, player's handbook, a setting overview — PDF, .txt, .md, .json, .csv, .yaml and other text formats). The assistant uses them when generating lore and can search them in chat, but they never become world canon.

import.dialogTitle: Import document into the world graph
import.confirmBody: This reads the whole of "{{filename}}" and proposes entities and relationships for your review, in pages. Nothing is written to the world until you approve a page.
import.migrateDialogTitle: Migrate into the world graph with AI
import.migrateConfirmBody: This reads everything in "{{name}}" (journals, notes, characters) and proposes entities and relationships for your review, in pages. Nothing is written to the world until you approve a page. Unlike Import, this does not expect Loregraph's own format — use it to bring an existing project in.
import.approveAllHint: Commits this page and every remaining page without asking again for each one.
import.doneSummary_one: Done — {{count}} entity added to the world.
import.doneSummary_other: Done — {{count}} entities added to the world.
import.failed: The import failed — check the backend logs for details.

onboarding.restartBody: The running backend doesn't expose the AI Assistant API yet (the config endpoint returned 404). Restart it to pick up the new code:
onboarding.setupBody1: The assistant runs on your own LLM API key (BYOK) — your lore never leaves this machine except for the calls you make to your chosen provider. Current provider: {{provider}}.
onboarding.setupBody3: Then restart the backend. The key is masked in all logs and errors.
onboarding.codexBody: Sign in to ChatGPT in a separate tab. This OAuth flow uses an experimental, unsupported Codex interface.
onboarding.codexPending: Sign-in has not been confirmed yet. Complete it in the browser and try again.

assistant.emptyInviteEmptyWorld: Your world is empty. Describe it in a couple of sentences — the assistant will propose starting lore: locations, factions, characters and their connections. Nothing becomes canon without your approval. You can also just ask questions.
assistant.emptyInviteHasWorld: Ask about the world, ask it to expand a part of it, or add new lore — the assistant answers grounded in existing canon and proposes drafts for review.
assistant.inputPlaceholderBlocked: Finish reviewing the draft above first (approve / request changes / reject)
assistant.inputPlaceholderDefault: Ask about the world or request new lore… (Enter to send)
assistant.attachTitle: Attach a file to this message (image, PDF, text) — drag and drop or paste from the clipboard (Ctrl+V)
assistant.hintIsolatedInstruction: Weave «{{title}}» into the world: figure out who and what connects to it, and add the missing entities and relationships.

review.newBadgeTitle: Entirely new — not based on existing lore
review.feedbackPlaceholder: What should change? E.g. "make the guild sinister, give it a secret leader"

review.groundedIn_other: Grounded in {{count}} fragments of existing lore

warnings.budget_exhausted: Token budget for this run is exhausted — generation stopped early.
warnings.mentions_existing: The request mentions existing entity «{{title}}» ({{type}}) — the draft should connect to it, not duplicate it.
warnings.duplicate_in_batch: The draft contains two near-identical titles: «{{title_a}}» and «{{title_b}}».
warnings.dropped_unknown_source: Dropped a relationship: its source ({{ref}}) is neither a draft entity nor retrieved lore.
warnings.dropped_unknown_target: Dropped a relationship: its target ({{ref}}) is neither a draft entity nor retrieved lore.
warnings.uncited_lore_id: The draft cites lore id {{id}} that was never retrieved — treat the related claim as unverified.
warnings.import_linked_existing: «{{title}}» linked to existing entity ({{existing_id}}) instead of creating a duplicate.
warnings.import_merged_duplicate: «{{title}}» merged with another occurrence of the same entity elsewhere in the document.
warnings.import_relationship_unresolved: Dropped a relationship that couldn't be resolved ({{source}} → {{target}}).
warnings.dropped_unknown_edge: Dropped a "{{op}}" operation: relationship ({{ref}}) was not among the ones shown.
warnings.dropped_self_relationship: Dropped a relationship from an entity ({{ref}}) to itself.
warnings.dropped_draft_entity: Dropped the new entity "{{title}}": this step only changes relationships.
warnings.relationship_scope_empty: Fewer than two of the requested entities exist — nothing to connect.
warnings.conflicting_relationship: These entities are already "{{existing_type}}", but "{{proposed_type}}" is proposed.
warnings.duplicate_relationship: A "{{type}}" relationship between these entities already exists.

events.batch_rejected: Draft rejected — nothing was written to the world.

integrations.heading: Integrations
integrations.hint: Connect external tools — an Obsidian vault, a Foundry VTT world, LongStoryShort character sheets, or any MCP server — to move content between Loregraph and the rest of your table. Each connection only offers what its tool can actually do.
integrations.noConnections: No connections yet. Add one to get started.
integrations.grounding: Let the assistant read this source
integrations.groundingHint: While generating lore, the assistant may look up current facts here (party sheets, world data) and use them as context. Nothing is written back.
integrations.autoPushHint: Every time you approve a proposal, the entities it touched are exported here as well. You can always export by hand instead.

typeHint.obsidian: Reads and writes Markdown notes in a vault folder on this machine.
typeHint.foundry: Talks to a running Foundry VTT world through the local bridge — journals, actors and scenes.
typeHint.longstoryshort: Imports character sheets exported from longstoryshort.app. No settings needed.
typeHint.mcp: Any MCP server you trust. The assistant gets its tools verbatim, exactly as when you connect one to an AI coding agent.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: A quick tour of how Loregraph is put together and how to work with it.

basics.title: Basics
basics.lead: Projects, entities and their fields — the building blocks of every world.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: A project is a separate world or campaign: its own entities, relationships, knowledge base and assistant settings. Switch between projects from the sidebar header.

entities.title: Entities
entities.body: NPCs, locations, factions, items, sessions — any piece of lore. Every entity has a type, a title, and a free-form set of fields.

fields.title: Fields
fields.body: Text, rich text, number or tags — the field type is up to you. Mark a field "on card" to show it right on the entity's graph card.

icons.title: Icons
icons.body: Upload an image and crop it right in the editor — the icon shows up on the entity's card in the graph and the list.

graph.title: Graph
graph.lead: The visual map of your world and its connections.

modes.title: Focused vs. All
modes.body: Focused mode shows one root entity's neighborhood up to a chosen depth — easier to read for large worlds. All mode draws the entire graph at once.

navigating.title: Navigating
navigating.body: Click a node to open its detail panel. Double-click or "Set as root" moves the graph's focus onto that entity.

filters.title: Filters
filters.body: Limit the visible relationship types and traversal depth from the filter dock at the bottom — it keeps dense graphs readable.

assistant.title: AI Assistant
assistant.lead: A co-author that answers questions about your world and proposes new lore.

setup.title: Setup
setup.body: The assistant needs a configured LLM provider (an API key) in the backend configuration — without one, the panel shows setup instructions.

chat.title: Chat
chat.body: Ask questions about the world, attach files, or pick an entity as context — the assistant answers grounded in the lore that already exists.

review.title: Draft review
review.body: New lore always comes up for approval: accept it, send it back with feedback, or reject the draft before it ever lands in the world.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.lead: Reference material the assistant draws on.

upload.title: Uploading documents
upload.body: Upload PDF, markdown or plain-text files (rulebooks, setting bibles) in project settings — the assistant uses them as reference context.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.lead: Exchanging content with external DM tools. "Integrations" in the left rail.

obsidian.title: Obsidian
obsidian.body: Export entities to a markdown vault with relationships as [[wikilinks]], or import notes back into the project.

foundry.title: Foundry VTT
foundry.body: Connects via the Foundry MCP bridge: export entities as journals/actors, or let the assistant use the live world state as context.

lss.title: Long Story Short
lss.body: "Import character sheets" on the Entities page takes the .json files a party exported from longstoryshort.app — drop in all of them at once. Each character arrives with the character-sheet template applied, and importing the same file again refreshes that character instead of duplicating it, keeping any fields you added yourself.

switches.title: The two switches on a connection
switches.body: "Let the assistant read this source" lets lore generation look up current facts there (a Foundry world, imported party sheets) and use them as context — it never writes anything back. "Export automatically after approval" sends every proposal you approve on to that tool as well. Each switch only appears on connections that can actually do it.

settings.title: Project settings
settings.lead: Fine-tuning the assistant's behavior and project maintenance.

instructions.title: Assistant instructions
instructions.body: Free-form notes on style, tone and format — blended into the lore-generation and chat system prompts for this project.

reindex.title: Reindexing
reindex.body: Rebuilds the lore search vector index from the current entity state — useful after a bulk import.
